subject: Atlas Payments go-live: rate-limit safety checks & ramp guidance
messages:
From: Todd Nguyen <todd.nguyen@atlas-payments.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Atlas go-live canary results — spike in 5xx/timeout at 1.2k QPS

Hi Sean / Monica,

We ran the canary traffic profile you suggested (50k users, 10k rps peak, client concurrency ramp) against our production integration this morning and saw a sharp uptick in 5xx and timeouts when sustained QPS crossed ~1,200. Attached is the raw canary_results.csv and a screenshot of the SLO dashboard. Error mix was roughly 60% 5xx (internal server errors), 25% timeouts, 15% 429.

We’re paused on the customer-facing go-live until we understand whether this is a client-side retry storm or an origin capacity issue on Redwood. We need a short exec note for our CTO and a clear list of immediate mitigations we can apply (client-side + Redwood config) before we resume.

Notes: some requests show repeated retries from our SDK with no jitter; we can patch the client quickly if you recommend new backoff params. Also curious whether a smaller model variant would reduce request CPU and improve tail latencies.

Can you triage and propose an emergency plan? Jenna (CC) is coordinating the internal Atlas launch logistics.

Thanks,
Todd
Todd Nguyen
Head of Integrations, Atlas Payments
Attachment: canary_results.csv (text/csv)
Attachment: slo_dashboard.png (image/png)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Todd Nguyen <todd.nguyen@atlas-payments.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas go-live canary results — spike in 5xx/timeout at 1.2k QPS

Todd — thanks for the quick data and the attachments. I reviewed the CSV and the dashboard snapshot. High-level plan below (short-term + next 24h). I’ll loop infra and product immediately.

Immediate actions (apply within 30–60m):
- Set Atlas’s client SDK to conservative retry/backoff: max_retries=2, base_backoff=300ms, jitter=full.
- Request Atlas to reduce client concurrency per connection: max_inflight_per_client=4 while we stabilize (we can relax later).
- Enable Redwood emergency scaling policy for this account: +20% reserved burst capacity and pre-warm KV caches for the model endpoints used in the canary.
- Activate model fallback to the lighter quantized variant for the first 5% of traffic (canary) to reduce per-request CPU.

Operational asks from us to Atlas: provide the exact QPS curve (1-minute granularity) you plan for the first 2 hours of go-live; confirm whether payment runtimes can tolerate the slower model variant for the canary.

I’m also attaching a quick ramp_playbook_v1.pdf with configuration snippets.

I’ll send an internal note with owners. Monica — can you own client SDK backoff guidance? Karthik — need a quick assessment on whether the 5xxs are originating from model OOMs, GPU queuing, or Redis/ingest timeouts. Evelyn — monitor SLOs and pre-prepare an exec summary. Rishi — please stand by for an emergency capacity bump.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ramp_playbook_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Atlas canary — owners & immediate tasks

Team — copying the canary artifacts from Atlas. TL;DR: 5xx/timeouts spike at ~1.2k QPS. Atlas will pause public go-live until we provide mitigations and an exec note for their CTO. Please see tasks below and confirm ETA in 15m.

Owners/tasks:
- Monica (support/SDK): Draft a one-page SDK change with exact values (max_retries, backoff, jitter, max_inflight_per_client) and a one-line patch Atlas can roll out in <30m.
- Karthik (serving/runtime): Run a focused triage on the canary timeframe for: model OOMs, request queue depth, GPU scheduling latency, and Redis/ingest timeouts. Return root-cause candidate + recommended config change (queue limits, token caps, model fallback) within 45m.
- Evelyn (SRE/observability): Assemble an exec-ready 1-slide summary (impact, current traffic, 5xx/% by minute, recommended short-term mitigations) for Atlas CTO. Include a link to our dashboard.
- Rishi (capacity/infra): Prepare a plan for emergency +20% burst capacity for Atlas and feasibility of routing 5% of traffic to dedicated nodes. Include estimated minutes-to-availability.

Keep replies short — we need a single consolidated action email to Atlas and the exec note in under 90 minutes.

Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Atlas canary — owners & immediate tasks

Quick triage notes (first-pass, based on logs during the stated window):
- Symptom: request queue latency climbs sharply after sustained QPS > 1,200; concurrent inflight tokens spike and GPU scheduling latency increases -> upstream requests time out.
- Root-cause candidates (likely order):
  1) Client retry storm amplifying burst pattern (observed repeated identical request IDs in 1m window).
  2) GPU scheduler saturation due to large-context requests (avg seq len higher than expected).
  3) Redis KV cache cold misses for prefix caching increasing tail latency.

Short-term mitigations I can apply now (no code deploy):
- Enforce per-account inflight cap: account.max_inflight = 1200 total; per-ip max_inflight_per_client = 4.
- Activate aggressive early-429 backoff: retry_policy = {"max_retries":"2","initial_backoff_ms":"300","max_backoff_ms":"2000","jitter":"full"}.
- Route 5% traffic to quantized model variant (lower memory) and enable reduced max_seq_length for canary.
- Prefill KV cache for hot prefixes (warmup API call).

Notes: the backoff/retry_policy above is our recommended safe default for SDK consumers; it reduces amplification and gives time for autoscaler to react. We should also instrument a small circuit-breaker to return a 503 quickly when queue depth exceeds a threshold.

ETA: can apply per-account caps + backoff policy in ~12 minutes. Model-fallback routing needs ~25 minutes to validate and pre-warm. Rishi — if you can confirm burst allocation we can bring +20% online in ~18 minutes.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Todd Nguyen <todd.nguyen@atlas-payments.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas go-live canary results — spike in 5xx/timeout at 1.2k QPS

Thanks — this helps a lot. Two asks from our side: 1) please send the exec-ready 1-slide summary to our CTO (cc’d) and 2) can Redwood run the adjusted canary (your backoff + per-client cap + 5% fallback model) on our behalf? We want to see the stabilized SLO curve before we let the marketing launch proceed.

We’ll patch our SDK concurrently to adopt the new backoff params. If Redwood can run the adjusted canary and share the results (CSV + dashboard snapshot), that would be ideal. Also include an ETA for when the emergency +20% capacity would be in place — our CTO asked specifically.

-Todd

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Todd Nguyen <todd.nganguyen@atlas-payments.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas go-live canary results — adjusted canary plan & exec note

Todd / Jenna — brief exec note below for your CTO and the actions we’ve taken. We’ll run the adjusted canary now and share results as CSV + dashboard link once complete (ETA ~45 minutes).

Executive summary for Atlas CTO (one-line): Redwood observed amplification from client retries and queue saturation at ~1.2k QPS; immediate mitigations (per-account inflight caps, conservative retry/backoff, 5% model fallback, +20% emergency burst capacity) are in place and we are executing an adjusted canary to validate stability before public go-live.

What we changed (already applied):
- Client guidance: max_retries=2, base_backoff=300ms, jitter=full; recommended client concurrency reduced to 4 inflight requests.
- Redwood runtime: account.max_inflight=1200, per-client max_inflight_per_client=4; early-429 backoff policy enabled.
- Routing: 5% of traffic directed to quantized model variant; KV prefix warm-up performed.
- Capacity: Rishi has enabled the emergency +20% burst pool (available in ~18 minutes).

Next steps: Redwood will run the adjusted canary and provide a CSV + dashboard snapshot. If SLOs stabilize (target: p99 latency < 450ms, 5xx < 0.5%), Atlas can proceed with a phased 2-hour ramp: 10% → 30% → 60% → 100% with 20-minute holds and monitoring gates.

We’ll share the canary outputs in ~45 minutes. Sending this to your CTO now.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ramp_playbook_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
